content: Telotristat ethyl interacts with various drugs by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which can reduce the systemic exposure and efficacy of drugs metabolized by this enzyme. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider alternative therapy if necessary. 2. Lefamulin: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining lefamulin with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers unless benefits outweigh risks. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 3. Lemborexant: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Lenacapavir: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Use an alternative drug. 5. Leniolisib: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 6. Levamlodipine: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Use caution and monitor blood pressure closely. No quantitative data is available on the effects of CYP3A4 inducers on amlodipine. 7. Lonafarnib: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated due to its sensitivity as a CYP3A4 substrate. 8. Lorlatinib: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor liver enzymes (ALT, AST, bilirubin) as recommended. 9. Lumateperone: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Lurbinectedin: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Mavacamten: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Coadministration is contraindicated. 12. Midazolam: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate if suboptimal efficacy is observed. 13. Naldemedine: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling suggests moderate CYP3A4 inducers reduce naldemedine exposure, but the clinical consequence is unknown. 14. Nirogacestat: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Norgestrel: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider additional barrier contraceptive methods. 16. Octreotide: Short-acting octreotide decreases telotristat ethyl levels. Administer octreotide at least 30 minutes after telotristat ethyl. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Olutasidenib: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers decrease olutasidenib plasma concentrations and efficacy. 18. Omaveloxolone: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Palovarotene: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Pemigatinib: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 21. Pimozide: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate if suboptimal efficacy is observed. 22. Pirtobrutinib: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, increase the pirtobrutinib dose as recommended. 23. Praziquantel: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Pretomanid: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 25. Quinidine: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate if suboptimal efficacy is observed. 26. Quinine: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate if suboptimal efficacy is observed. 27. Quizartinib: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Repotrectinib: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Rimegepant: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Ripretinib: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration is unavoidable, increase dosing frequency as recommended. 31. Selumetinib: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Siponimod: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended for certain genotypes. 33. Sirolimus: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate if suboptimal efficacy is observed. 34. Stiripentol: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Use caution and monitor closely if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inducer. 35. Sufentanil: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers may decrease sufentanil levels, potentially causing withdrawal syndrome in dependent patients. 36. Tacrolimus: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate if suboptimal efficacy is observed. 37. Tazemetostat: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Theophylline: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate if suboptimal efficacy is observed. 39. Tinidazole: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Tivozanib: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Triazolam: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate if suboptimal efficacy is observed. 42. Ubrogepant: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Dose adjustment is recommended with concomitant use of moderate and weak CYP3A4 inducers. 43. Voclosporin: Telotristat ethyl reduces its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Zuranolone: Telotristat ethyl decreases its levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Adverse Effects: Common side effects include nausea (13%), headache (11%), increased GGT (9%), depression (9%), peripheral edema (7%), flatulence (7%), decreased appetite (7%), pyrexia (7%), abdominal pain (5%), and constipation (5%). Less common effects include increased alkaline phosphatase, ALT, and AST (<5%), intestinal obstruction, angioedema, pruritus, and rash. Serious complications of constipation have been reported. Monitor for severe or worsening abdominal pain and discontinue if necessary. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: No human data are available to assess drug-associated risks during pregnancy. Unknown if distributed in human breast milk. Consider the benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother’s clinical need for the drug and potential adverse effects on the infant. Monitor infants for constipation if administered to breastfeeding women. Administration and Storage: Take with food. Store at controlled room temperature (25°C [77°F]), with excursions permitted to 15–30°C (59–86°F). When used with short-acting octreotide, administer octreotide at least 30 minutes after telotristat ethyl.
